test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Two Statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All pens are cars.

Some cars are bulbs.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some cars are not bulbs.

II. Some pens being bulbs is a possibility.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

solution:
Given Statements:

All pens are cars.

Some cars are bulbs.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f572ce51e352a2fb49988f1e34b8d2de220601ac12c5510312ec51cecfdd40ab.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some cars are not bulbs - False (Because, Some cars are bulbs doesn't gives definite relation of the remaining part of cars to bulb, so it can be possible only).

II. Some pens being bulbs is a possibility - True (Because, No definite relation given between Pens and Bulbs, so it can be possible that some pens are bulbs).

So, Only conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
